title: On the Hardness of Reinforcement Learning with Transition Look-Ahead
abstract: arXiv:2510.19372v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study reinforcement learning (RL) with transition look-ahead, where the agent may observe which states would be visited upon playing any sequence of $\ell$ actions before deciding its course of action. While such predictive information can drastically improve the achievable performance, we show that using this information optimally comes at a potentially prohibitive computational cost. Specifically, we prove that optimal planning with one-step look-ahead ($\ell=1$) can be solved in polynomial time through a novel linear programming formulation. In contrast, for $\ell \geq 2$, the problem becomes NP-hard. Our results delineate a precise boundary between tractable and intractable cases for the problem of planning with transition look-ahead in reinforcement learning.

translated_title: 论带转移前瞻的强化学习的计算困难性
translated_abstract: 我们研究具有转移前瞻的强化学习（RL），其中智能体可以在决定其行动方案之前，观察到执行任意 ℓ 个动作序列后将会访问哪些状态。虽然这种预测信息能够大幅提升可实现的性能，但我们证明最优地利用这些信息可能伴随着极高的计算代价。具体而言，我们证明了带一步前瞻（ℓ=1）的最优规划问题可以通过一种新颖的线性规划表述在多项式时间内求解。相比之下，当 ℓ ≥ 2 时，该问题变为NP-难问题。我们的结果为强化学习中带转移前瞻的规划问题划定了可解与不可解情形之间的精确边界。
tldr: 该论文通过新颖的线性规划方法证明带一步前瞻的强化学习最优规划可在多项式时间内求解，而两步及以上前瞻的规划问题是NP难的，从而精确划定了该问题的可解与不可解边界。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that optimal planning with one-step transition look-ahead in RL is solvable in polynomial time via a novel linear programming formulation, while for two or more steps of look-ahead the problem becomes NP-hard, delineating a precise tractability-intractability boundary.
